0.x: **Montagu Declaration, 20 August 1917:** "progressive realisation of **responsible government** in India as an integral part of the British Empire" – the first official promise; pressure mainly from the **Home Rule Leagues**.
**Edwin Montagu** = Secretary of State for India; **Lord Chelmsford** = Viceroy; the **Montagu-Chelmsford Report, 1918** (**constitutional reforms**) was the **basis of the GoI Act, 1919**.
Passed **1919**, in force **1921**; British PM: **David Lloyd George** (1916-22). The Morley-Minto Act is the separate **Indian Councils Act, 1909**.

r: **Central and provincial subjects separated** ("Devolution Rules") – jurisdiction of Centre and provinces clearly defined; **devolution of legislative authority** to provinces
Still **centralised and unitary** despite devolution; a large part of authority delegated to provinces
**Dyarchy** (reserved / transferred) and extension of provincial government; provincial budgets **separated** from the central budget
**Bicameral** for the first time: **Council of State** (60) + **Legislative Assembly** (145, 104 elected) – **expanded and reconstituted legislatures**
**Direct elections** for the first time (1909 = indirect); franchise limited by property, tax, education
Communal representation **extended** – separate electorates for **Sikhs**, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans (Muslim separate electorates = **1909**)
3 of the 6 members (other than the C-in-C) Indian
New office of **High Commissioner for India**, London; first holder Sir William Meyer
**Section 96(C)** → Public Service Commission; set up **1926** (Lee Commission)
**Statutory commission after 10 years** → Simon Commission (1927, two years early)
No term fixed by the Act; governors (like the Governor-General) appointed for **five years** by practice

0.x: Congress special **Bombay session, Aug 1918 (Hasan Imam)** condemned the scheme; **Amritsar (1919)**: "inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing".
Moderates under **Surendranath Banerjee** (with Sapru, Srinivasa Sastri, Jayakar) left and formed the **Indian (National) Liberal Federation** (1919).
**C.R. Das + Tilak** rejected it; **Gandhi + Malaviya**: give it a fair trial; **Krishna Patrika**: "giving with the right hand, taking with the left".

**Andhra:** **Nyapati Subbarao**'s 27-member Andhra delegation met Montagu at Madras for an **Andhra province**; **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** presided over the Special Andhra Mahasabha, **Guntur, 17 Aug 1918**.
**Muddiman Committee (1924):** the British response to the **Swarajist** demand for a review of the 1919 Act.

3.x: First elections **1920** under the 1919 Act; the **Congress boycotted** them (Non-Cooperation).
**Justice Party won 63 seats** → first ministry under **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** (Dec 1920), then **Raja of Panagal** (1921).

r: **1923, 1926, 1930, 1934, 1945** – **last in 1945**; the **1937** (provincial) elections were under the **1935 Act**
Won **42 of 104** elected seats; worked with independents like **Jinnah** and Malaviya
Swarajist, elected **President (Speaker)** in **August 1925** – the first Indian
**V. Ramadas** elected to the Central Legislative Assembly (1923)
**Rowlatt (Sedition) Committee** under **Sir Sidney Rowlatt**; replaced the wartime **Defence of India Act** with a permanent law
Arrest on suspicion, **detention without trial** (up to two years), trial without jury
**"Black Act" / "Black Bill"** (Gandhi: "Black Law"); "No Vakil, No Appeal, No Daleel"
**Rowlatt Satyagraha** – nationwide hartal **6 April 1919**; **Jallianwala Bagh, 13 April 1919**; satyagraha suspended **18 April 1919**
